input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
input.rationale: Paragraph 4(a) sits at the fallback for our side: after the one-year Initial Term we may terminate for any reason on ninety (90) days' notice (the Initial Term lock-in is exactly 12 months, so it is noted rather than flagged), and the only termination-related payment is Kubient's entitlement to fees generated during the 90-day termination period, i.e. no early-termination fee beyond three months of fees. The clause fails the fallback on one material term: the same for-any-reason right lets Kubient walk mid-term during any renewal period, and the effective date is not tied to the end of the then-current term, so this is a Vendor mid-term convenience exit rather than natural-term non-renewal. Our single edit limits Kubient's for-any-reason termination to the end of a term, leaving our right and the 90-day notice period verbatim.

ops.newText: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party; provided Kubient may terminate only at the end of a term.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 90 days' notice each way works for us, but we cannot accept Kubient exiting mid-term, so we have limited its for-any-reason termination to the end of a term while leaving our own right and the notice period untouched.
proposal.summary: Limit Kubient's convenience termination to the end of a term
